title: Strict-local base-change is invertible on global homology for a chosen model
statement: Let f:X→S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], s:Spec Ω→S a geometric point over an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and A a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let eA:Spec A≅strictHenselizationScheme(s) [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let sq₀ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with maps p₀:X₀→X and f₀:X₀→Spec A over f and eA.hom followed by strictHenselizationStructuralMap(s) [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. For every bounded-below derived abelian etale sheaf K [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] and integer n, global sections on Spec A of Hⁿ of the derived base-change mate of sq₀ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] are invertible. This does not assert invertibility of the sheaf morphism or of its stalks.

proof.text: Steps 1–3 of the parent proof. Identify the canonical derived mate with derivedBaseChangeMapPlus by derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_ext and derivedPlus_mateEquiv_app_fac. Lift the chosen cartesian model to the canonical pullback. Pullback cancellation gives a cartesian comparison square with bottom edge eA.hom, so its upper edge is invertible. Exact inverse-image equivalences preserve injectives, and calculation on injective representatives makes the comparison-square derived mate invertible. Apply horizontal pasting to express the chosen mate as comparison isomorphisms, the pullback of the canonical mate, and the comparison-square mate. Homology commutes with exact inverse image. Global sections after inverse image along eA.hom are naturally isomorphic to original sections, using the invertible unit and lowerStarCompGlobalSectionsIso. Thus the canonical factor is invertible after global homology by the existing strict-local global-homology theorem, and every other factor is an image of an isomorphism. Their composite is invertible.
